rows.text: The Lance of Fury once became the Mad King, plunging the world into ceaseless strife, until your valor brought it to an end.
Back then, the Incarnation of Time entrusted Mem to you at the Temple of the Three Fates. Back then, the lively girl with red hair fulfilled her mission, and bid the first farewell.
Not long ago, the head of the Grove Sages helped you repel the menace that is the black tide.
The prophecy once made the Hand of Shadow choose two people, granting one the fate of death. Yet their bond wove a hauntingly beautiful tale that stretched across time.

Time and again, farewells haven't numbed you. You can't help but wonder — how many more goodbyes will the journey of "Trailblazing" entail? You question whether you'll be able to express each "goodbye" with heartfelt emotion.
What a long journey it's been...
"Strife"...
"Time"...
"Reason"...
"Death"...
You must admit that some people still manage to live joyfully at this arduous low point in life. Cipher's endless desires for wealth seem more turbulent than the waters of Scalegorge Waterscape.
Forget the past for now — it only brings sorrow. But sadness has no place in this moment. What you need is the drive to move forward.
You decide to head to Styxia, where the River of Souls is no longer blocked, to meet up with that catgirl. Hopefully, those glittering, clinking trinkets will, as always... lift your spirits.
...Styxia's moonlight is so beautiful.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: And the River of Souls is so quiet... It's like everything that happened was just a dream. I wonder if Cas is doing okay on the other side? If I write a letter and put it in a drift bottle, will she be able to read it?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I miss Castorice too...
Now's not the time to feel down.
No. No! This shouldn't be so depressing!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ... You're right. We promised Cas that we'd continue the Flame-Chase Journey, so we can't let her worry.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: By the way, it was Miss Cipher who asked us to come here, but where has she gone...?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...Huh?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: What's that sound?
Is there someone else here?
I don't know, but this aura... feels so familiar.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Yes, and this aura... feels so familiar.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ... [Trailblazer], let's go check it out together. Be very careful...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I... I have a bad feeling about this.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Hey, what's that on the ground? Should we pick it up...?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Careful... Careful...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: It's... a piece of black cloth?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Now, where have I seen this before...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: It's the Flame Reaver...
Did someone rip off a piece of my clothes?
Wh—What? How could they be here?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Wha— No. Your clothes are perfectly fine!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Could this be from... the Flame Reaver's cloak!? Why is it here?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Mem! Memi!!!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: — [Trailblazer], look out!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Now's not the time to feel down. We gotta pull ourselves together!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Mem, get ready —
Now's not the time to feel down. We gotta pull ourselves together!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: You want the pink puppy, don't you?
Is it finally time... for me to bow out?
Wait! We both know what this thing can do...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I — What? Now I'm sad! This isn't the time for jokes —
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: D—Don't give up just like that!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Let's try our best to deal with them for now, and we'll slip into the past with Time's power as soon as we can!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: The River of Souls...
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: Is full of fish... Big and delicious.
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: What.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: The Flame-Chase Journey... stops...
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: Meow... meow...
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: M—Meow?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...What's happening?
Is this meant to be a riddle?
The Flame Reaver's gone mad. The end.
I—I don't understand this language at all. Am I hallucinating...?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: W—We already knew about the mad part! But are we still in danger...?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Hehehe... hehehehehe...
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: ...Hehehahahahahahha!
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: Ahahahahaha... Sorry. I couldn't pass on the chance to give you two a good scare!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: So it's you! Cipher!
What a terrible person. Let's leave.
This Cipher must be fake too. Run!
Ah! Don't run! I'm the real Cipher! The real one!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: C'mon, don't be upset. I'm just giving you a kind reminder that Amphoreus isn't safe at all. The whole place is full of dangers, including that swordmaster... Make sure you stay on your toes, no matter where you are!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: So you're playing both good cop and bad cop.
Well, ain't I grateful for the reminder.
I'm so strong that I don't need your reminder.
Hey, I'm just making it up to you. You'd do the same in my shoes.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Hey, I'm just making it up to you. You're not gonna hold that over me, are you?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Really? But just a minute ago that gray hair of yours was all standing up, you were so scared.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: So... was that a Flame Reaver disguise? Or a magic trick? It looked so real... Is that the power of the Trickery demigod?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Disguise? No no no, it's not as simple as that. Lemme think about how to explain this...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: For example, what did you think when you realized that piece of cloth came from the Flame Reaver's cloak?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Hmm... We thought that maybe the Flame Reaver was around here somewhere?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: That's right. And then you heard some footsteps. What did you think when that happened?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Well, we thought it must be the Flame Reaver coming this way...?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Yep, exactly. I just used some hints and mental suggestions to help you believe in a lie...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: "Lies" are what Zagreus is best at. If everyone believes in a lie, then it becomes reality!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: A power to make lies into reality... That's got all my hairs standing up!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Nice! Now I know your secret!
And... you're just telling us everything like that?
I sure love your arrogance, Gray Mystery~
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: You think I might be lying? Pfft. No need.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: The seamstress trusts you for a reason. Someone as honest as you couldn't trick me even if you wanted to, so there's no harm in telling you.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Besides, we still need to team up to go treasure hunting, right? Let's wrap up here. It's time to get going~
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: ...Oh? Was that your teleslate?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Heh, aren't you a popular one? But I got to you first, so help me with the treasures, and then I'll send you two to the Grove.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Why do you need so much money anyway?
Gonna go live handsomely somewhere after this?
Curiosity killed the cat, you know? Do you think I'll spend it all? Pfft. That's so not why I hunt for treasures.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Live handsomely? You mean, spend all this money? Pfft. That's so not why I hunt for treasures.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Don't forget. I'm a demigod too, and there's a line reserved for me in that stupid prophecy as well... "You shall walk with greed, and die over petty change."
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: But I don't believe in that. As long as I keep collecting treasures, then I won't need to care about petty change. And as long as I don't hurt other people when I get what I want, I won't be "walking with greed" — right? Isn't that simple?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: So, as long as I keep going down this path... all those predestined prophecies and fates will never catch up to me!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Phew. That was a long speech. I'm getting thirsty at this rate! The treasures of Styxia aren't gonna float up on their own. Come on, Gray Mystery, show me what the authority of "Time" can do!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: A few days later, at the crash site in the Abyss of Fate...
...So, this is the car of the Astral Express you've spoken of. My repository of memories has been enriched with another fascinating piece of information. Thank you for leading me here, Lord Dan Heng.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I'm surprised a Council Elder like yourself would be willing to journey so far to inspect the Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Okhemans hold wisdom and knowledge in high esteem. If the citizens knew of your origins, I'm sure more would be intrigued by "the Trailblaze." Sadly, discussions about the "world beyond the sky" remain taboo.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: It's been quite some time since you first arrived in Okhema. Presumably you've been looking for a way to leave ever since?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I've been actively gathering clues and testing different things. Sadly, the more I find out, the more powerless I feel.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Don't be too hard on yourself, my lord. This puzzle has stumped Amphoreus's scholars for centuries. It isn't something you can solve overnight... even someone as gifted as yourself.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: In the Grove, I discovered extensive research on the Sky Titan. It appears that many scholars from Amphoreus believe the taboo against the "world beyond the sky" stems from a curse cast by Aquila.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Exactly. Of the Twelve Titans of Amphoreus, Aquila is known for being the most capricious.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: The weather itself reflects their mood: Tranquil sunshine, mournful rain. Aquila's breath is a brisk wind, and their cries resound as thunder in a storm.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: ...That's it? Nothing else?
After finishing this mind-shaking piece, only one image remains in your mind...
Invigorating literature, your favorite.
Additionally, Aquila is one of the two Titans whose Coreflames have yet to be returned.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The sky above affects every citizen. It's clear that Lady Aglaea's decision to confront Aquila at the end of the Flame-Chase Journey was a carefully considered strategy.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: If returning Aquila's Coreflame can break the sky's curse, we won't have to exhaust ourselves searching for a way back. We can simply focus on aiding the Chrysos Heirs.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Antikytherans have no home to return to, so I understand your concern for your old friends and homeland.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I used Antikytheran technology — or "scanning," as you might call it — to assess this car. Assuming my judgment is correct, I might be able to conduct a thorough overhaul of its "power systems."
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Really? But...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Of course, that's only if you, my lord, permit me to interact with it.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: ...By all means, please proceed. But be careful, the Express's thrusters are extremely delicate.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You honor me with your trust. I will be very careful.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Lygus carefully scans the damaged propulsion system, then methodically began inspecting its components...
This... is unbelievable. You seem to understand its structure perfectly. Have you repaired something like this before?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Not exactly. But we Antikytherans are inherently sensitive to machinery. Kephale endowed our kind with a unique advantage for analyzing and learning.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: If you give me some time, I might be able to fully restore this damaged car to its former glory. Then you and your esteemed companion could set off on your return journey sooner.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: But... isn't the real issue with Aquila?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Your friend seems quite interested in us. Perhaps you could explain, Lord Phainon? It would be the polite thing...
rows.speaker: "Cleaner" Captain

rows.text: Hypothetically, Lord Dan Heng, if I could open up a path out of Amphoreus that circumvents Aquila's divine punishment...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Would you consider ceasing your support for the Flame-Chase Journey?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I don't understand... Does the Council of Elders possess some secret means of counteracting divine punishment?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's best if you don't delve too deeply into that question, my lord. All you need to know is, I can make it happen.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: (Maybe this is not a decision by the Council of Elders but rather his personal wish...)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The crucial point is, if you and your companion are unwilling to halt your support for the Chrysos Heirs... it could offend certain interests.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Hmm...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Forgive me, Lord Lygus, but I must be frank. When visiting Dawncloud, I reviewed the records of many Council Elders...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Among them, only your background was nearly blank. I'd like to accept your goodwill, but given such a mysterious background and motives, anyone cautious would have doubts.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Your prudence impresses me, just as expected...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Are these people—
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Is this a trap? Is that why you accompanied me here?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Please don't misunderstand, Lord Dan Heng. As the Theoros, I have no allegiance to their plans nor am I obliged to obstruct them. I am neutral.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Out of respect for you, I hope to offer a peaceful solution to ensure the safety of you and your companion.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: ...One against four, then.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Just to confirm: if things turn ugly later... will you help?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I will not. As I said, I remain neutral.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Are you asking this because you plan to refuse my offer and continue supporting the Chrysos Heirs?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You weren't wrong about one thing, Lord Lygus. Indeed, we must try to return to our companions...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: But our "companions" now also include the Flame-Chasing Chrysos Heirs. The Nameless cannot and will not ignore the fate of our companions.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: So I see. This is what you call "Trailblazing."
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: When I asked if you'd help, I meant...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...the ones who need help are them.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Meanwhile, in the Grove of Epiphany...
Tsk —
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You have such overwhelming power, so... why...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Answer me! Why do you stand in our way... Why do you want to take the Coreflames!?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Uwah —!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Oh no! He can't hold on anymore!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Drag him back here, friend!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Are you okay?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I'm okay. I can handle that kind of hit now. But a few months ago, that would've knocked me out.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Always keeping me on edge...
If I had passed out, that would've been it.
Thanks for worrying, buddy.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Ha... That's why I made sure you were well-fed and rested on the road.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Thanks for the help. To face Aquila and other potential threats, I must sharpen myself with the most aggressive methods.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Even so, it's impressive you thought of this training method. Battling the phantoms of the past in the river of time... It's just like the "Hyperbolic Time Sanctum" that the bards describe.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Ha, it's working pretty well, wouldn't you say?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But combat isn't just about strength and skill. You also need the right weapon. Compared to that guy's weapon, mine feels like I'm swinging a lump of iron. I can't tell you how many swords I've gone through since the training began.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Why not get Chartonus to help?
Weight training, huh?
Don't worry. I'm not wielding my sword for revenge. [Trailblazer]'s been through Nikador's trial and understands. Those who can't walk out of the shadows of their past are ultimately weak.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Don't worry. I've already arranged that. Of course I need him.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's a good thing Chartonus is the finest blacksmith in Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I asked him to make a suitable divine weapon for me. It's a little embarrassing to say this, but in order to help me, he deliberately turned down all other business.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Chartonus is part of this Flame-Chase Journey after all, full of energy!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Ha, thinking about how he's been recently... maybe you're right.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But, Phainon, I've been somewhat concerned about you...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Lately, you seem more and more fixated on that swordmaster in black.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: That's quite the sudden shift in topic.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I've been holding this question in for a long time! You're getting stronger, but seeds of unrest are also growing in me!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Times have changed. The responsibility I bear is both precious and fragile. I wield my sword for the future of Amphoreus. I will not let hatred cloud my judgment again and neglect my duties.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You've really grown.
But you can't beat them yet.
We'll be here by your side.
I'm far from finished. I must continue sharpening my skills... until I can match their strength.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Right, I must continue sharpening my skills... Eventually, I'll need to face them on the battlefield.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You're right, partner. As of now, I'm not able to handle that swordmaster on my own. I still need the help of my friends.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Huh... Every time I say something, things get so serious... I don't want to be the person who keeps bringing the mood down.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I'm out of energy for training today. How about we go to the Library of Philia to lighten the mood?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Sure, that's what I've been looking forward to! We deserve to enjoy ourselves after all the hard work.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: This historical perspective seems biased, glossing over the Chrysos Heirs' abuse of divine powers and their blatant initiation of war, in order to defame our predecessors...
rows.speaker: "Cleaner" Captain

rows.text: Today I'm definitely going to... hehe...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: What were you reading before?
Why not take the interesting ones home?
A girl's little secret. Don't pry.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Great idea! However, that would mean no more reasons to visit the Grove.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: That's the charm of this place. You can find whatever you're into here.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The three of us might not be into scholarly books, but we could still spend an entire day at the Library of Philia.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Here we are! Where was that slate last time? Was it here, or maybe over here...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I'm off to have some fun! It's free time now, so you should relax too.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Let's stop here...
Forbidden Love: The Tree and the Butterfly
One Punch God: Aquila
(Hmm... I wonder what Phainon and Mem are reading?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Just curious what you're reading.
Are you reading something you shouldn't be?
You could have just asked. There's nothing embarrassing about it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: In front of you all? That would be pretty careless.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Here, look, I'm reading this — Antiques Appraisal: How to Make a Fortune.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Didn't know you were into this.
I know how. In your dreams.
Maybe it's time to find a different side gig.
You didn't know? After all this time we've known each other, that pains me...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Your comments cut deep. It's tough to find a good comeback.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...No way, I've invested almost all my savings into this hobby!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I've spent a lot of time pondering how Aglaea became such an effective leader — beyond the intangible qualities like personality and ethics, a major reason is her family wealth!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That's the perk of growing up in a big city, isn't it? For those of us in the sticks? Luck doesn't come as easily. It's thirty percent grind, seventy percent fate...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Oops, talked too much. As a leader, you need both integrity and weal — I mean integrity and skill.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Are you into fishing?
Superstitions, superstitions, don't buy into them.
Whoa, you scared me!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: (Something's odd about Mem. What are they flipping through?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: "Ruler" fits me pretty well.
Use them flexibly. Don't just memorize.
Ah! [Trailblazer]? Hmm... What a coincidence! We meet again. Guess we're fated to be together, huh?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: (So suspicious, not like their usual self...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: A little faith in these things isn't bad sometimes.
It should be approached with a critical eye...
To me, divination could be a power that guides our spirits.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: You've really thought about this, haven't you?
What if divination predicts something bad?
After all, the first chapter of the "Divination Compendium" discusses "the significance of divination." I'm just expanding on that a bit!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Divination is only meaningful when there are both good and bad outcomes.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Those mitts up to the task?
Then, gotta craft a Mem-specific deck.
Oh, now that you mention it, yes! It would be even better if it were made of, say... crystal!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: You are...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Assassins. Save me!
Nice cosplay.
Eyes peeled, everyone.
These folks are up to no good...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Black clothing... Masks decorated with golden blood...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Are they "Cleaners"?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Ha... To directly call us by our name, it seems you, Lord Phainon, have studied the forgotten history of Amphoreus quite thoroughly.
rows.speaker: "Cleaner" Captain

rows.text: Who are they?
What's being cleaned? Clothes or cars?
...We can't let our esteemed guests pass away without understanding.
rows.speaker: "Cleaner" Captain

rows.text: During the Chrysos War, to combat the Chrysos Heirs, several cities formed an underground assassin squad called "the Cleaners."
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Their task was to erase anyone with golden blood from existence. Assassination, poisoning, political persecution... They would do anything to achieve their objective.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Could you disclose the name of the author behind this popular legend, Lord Phainon? I'd hate for the innocent children of Okhema to be tainted by such slanted narratives.
rows.speaker: "Cleaner" Captain

rows.text: You should have stayed buried in the dust of history. The citizens' assembly has once again legitimized the mission of the Chrysos Heirs, but as for you...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Not one citizen would cast their vote for you executioners lurking in the shadows.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What does it matter? We've long since stopped expecting to be understood...
rows.speaker: "Cleaner" Captain

rows.text: People have become too accustomed to peace... and they've forgotten the disasters that arose from allowing generations of the Chrysos Heirs to rule!
rows.speaker: "Cleaner" Captain

rows.text: Complete nonsense. Did you really travel all the way to the Grove just to have an argument?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I enjoy dealing with people as straightforward as you, Lord Phainon.
rows.speaker: "Cleaner" Captain

rows.text: You've probably figured out why we've come before you...
rows.speaker: "Cleaner" Captain

rows.text: Just a handful of you here. Who do you think you're fighting?
If it's a fight you want, let's get on with it — enough chit-chat!
Keep your cool, [Trailblazer]. They've come out of the shadows, which suggests they have something up their sleeves.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Alright, let's hear it — what are you hiding? But watch your language, and don't say anything you might regret.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: My shoulders might be sore and my sword a tad dull... but it's still enough to slice off your tongues.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Ah...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: How's it going, Cinny? This place fits, doesn't it?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: It's a bit small, but the lighting is perfect!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Thank you, Lady Tribbie! With this, the Twilight Courtyard can be reborn in Okhema.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Do you like it here too, Little Ica?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Doot... Doot-Doot!
rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: Hehe... It's so bright here, maybe you should rename it? How about "Luminous Courtyard"?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Lady Tribbie makes a good point. But... "Twilight Courtyard" carries the long history of the descendants of the sky, and I'd like it to continue.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Right... How does the legend go again? Hmm...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Heh... Even Lady Tribbie forgets things...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: ...We... We just haven't prepared lessons in a while now, so we're a bit rusty! Just give us some time, and we'll remember!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...Ah, now we remember! Kremnos and the Firmament, Volume 3, Section 5 —
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: "With Seliose, the Daythunder Knight, striking down the Eye of Twilight, the divine war between Nikador and Aquila, which spanned centuries, came to an end..."
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: "Thereafter... the Skyfolk gradually declined, numerous sky fortresses were abandoned, and their descendants began to establish themselves on the land..."
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: "Finally, those descended from Seliose the Daythunder Knight were welcomed by the scholars under Cerces and established the Twilight Courtyard in the Grove..."
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Hmm, the historical records seem slightly at odds with our memories... but the details from that time have become somewhat hazy to us.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Oh, I forgot... For Lady Tribbie, history is more than just words on a page — it's something you've personally lived through.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Doot! Doot-Doot, Doot!
rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: Heh, Little Ica loves listening to the stories from the legends. I'm sure you're also imagining, one day, you'll be as awe-inspiring as the winged beasts by Seliose's side?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: That day will come! I believe it! Just keep growing...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: ...Ah, Lord Krateros?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Miss Hyacine...
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: ...And Lady Tribbie, good to see you're doing alright. I heard from the citizens you were nearby and came to check.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Doing... alright? What's going on, Krateros?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: There's been another violent incident at the market. A shop was smashed and looted. It's the third time this week.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: How can this be? I always thought that with Lady Aglaea here, Okhema would remain peaceful...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: That was true in the past. But these days... forgive my bluntness, her senses may not be as sharp as they once were.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Agy...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: In my opinion, malevolent forces have noticed the slack in the golden threads and are now plotting to exploit the opportunity.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: The citizens' assembly just wrapped up... Why is there still unrest?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: The Chrysos Heirs won by only one vote, Lady Tribbie. From my years of experience, a narrow victory often walks hand-in-hand with unrest.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: ...Trouble! Miss Hyacine... trouble!
...Clementine? Take a breath... What's going on?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Please! Something terrible has happened at Marmoreal Palace!
rows.speaker: Clementine

rows.text: What is it, doctor? Calm yourself and talk us through!
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Lady Aglaea...
rows.speaker: Clementine

rows.text: It's... it's Lady Aglaea who's in trouble!
rows.speaker: Clementine

rows.text: Moments ago in Marmoreal Palace...
I still remember, this bath that overlooks the entire Palace was built by the Council of Elders nine hundred years ago.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Eh? Why did it suddenly stop?
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: *cough* ...Just a tiny hiccup. No worries. Let's try again.
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Slow down, Boss!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Your legs are long and mine are short!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Agy...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Its purpose was to commemorate the first Flame-Chase Journey, and to remember the heroes who made great sacrifices for Amphoreus a millennium ago.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Rules were set then. No one was allowed to enter, apart from guests invited by the Goldweaver.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I'll stay here to lead the guards and maintain order. Find out what happened — but don't take too long. With Aglaea gone, someone has to take her place and lead Okhema.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Also, Miss Hyacine was the one who declared Aglaea dead. You might want to speak with her.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Agy...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: So, you... really don't have to take the medicine anymore?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: No need, teacher. Medicine can only steady my flesh, but it cannot stop the decay of my soul.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I've already borrowed too much time from this world... And now, the time is up.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Now... is the best time for my exit.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: *sob*... *sniffle*...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Please don't cry on my account, teacher...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I have... a final selfish request. Can you lend me an ear?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: *sniffle* Agy...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Go ahead... *sob* We will... definitely fulfill it for you.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: I wish for my death to be quiet and gentle. I hope that my lifeless body... will not be exposed to the eyes of the public.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Teacher, I have faced too many changes in my lifetime. But in the pursuit of one thing alone, I have remained unchanged for a thousand years...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...It's "beauty," isn't it?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Huh...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: That's right, teacher. "Beauty."
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Agy, do you think Snowy is... ready?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: A thousand years ago, when I took up the Coreflame of Mnestia... do you think I was ready then, teacher?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Born into this era, we had no choice but to grow amidst the raging waves, not set sail after everything was prepared.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Phainon — he will understand. He will grasp the duty I've left to him... He is mature enough now, no longer blinded by anger or hatred.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: But, I guess... you're no longer pretending to follow the rules, are you, Lady Caenis?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Aglaea, Aglaea...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: You ageless witch, hiding behind a divine facade to deceive mortals... We've been far too kind with you.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Kind? There's no need to use such a word to cover up your...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Incompetence.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Anaxagoras humiliated all of you before the citizens. If you still had any shred of shame, you'd throw yourselves from Dawncloud at the Curtain-Fall Hour to salvage the last fragments of your dignity.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Demigod, why not gaze into the water's reflection and see the wretched face you wear now?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: I can't imagine, how she could've been taken down by a handful of assassins...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I hope so...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: If this is all part of a larger plan, Tribbie must know something. She just couldn't say it in the message.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I also don't understand... This doesn't add up.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No, that doesn't make sense...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The ones who appeared in the Grove, and those who confronted Dan Heng in the Abyss, didn't immediately resort to violence. They were just watching and trying to intimidate.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Not well. After all, we witnessed Lady Aglaea's... last moments.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Yes... we witnessed her final moments.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: I tried to treat her immediately, but even the sky's blessings...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: ...Chartonus?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Oh! Alright.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Indeed!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...You think highly of yourself, don't you?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: The Flame-Chase Journey is nearing its end, with only one Titan left for the Chrysos Heirs to conquer: {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: These days you're not only blind but also deaf... The "Cleaners" were born for this moment. When all orders, rules, and laws fail to restrain you, it's time for the dagger to pass judgment.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: If you're in such a hurry, give it a try.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Hmph... going toe-to-toe with a demigod? We're not that foolish.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: The dagger isn't at your throat, but...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Your gravest accusation is that my humanity is fading, and you claim my concern for mortal joys and sorrows is nothing but a facade.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: If that accusation holds... what makes you think the lives of these civilians will sway me in the slightest?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Fine. I'll gladly use a few more words to shatter that demigod facade of yours.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Like I said, you're not only blind but deaf too. Lately, your control over Okhema has weakened.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: You failed to notice the thefts we arranged in the market, nor did you catch wind of the meetings happening in the Dromas Workshop. Plots are unfolding right under your nose, yet you remain indifferent.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Humanity fading? Ha, Aglaea, why not use your precious golden thread to peer into my thoughts? See if the gift we've so meticulously prepared for you can move that cold demigod heart of yours.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: In this moment, I only regret not being more ruthless. Because your evil... is beyond cure.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...I wonder where [Trailblazer] is now. If they're targeting me, {F#s}he definitely won't escape their notice either. I hope all is well...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You finally figured it out? Ha... you have grown dull. I've been holding that image in my mind this whole time to make sure you could see it clearly.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: (I want you to have this knucklebone talisman, big sis. I hope it brings you luck every day and keeps you safe from bullies!)
rows.speaker: Silent Girl

rows.text: That girl who can't speak or hear... What if she accidentally lost her eyes too?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: You know better than anyone what it feels like to lose your sight. Imagine if a thousand years ago, you, already blind, had also lost your voice and hearing in your youth — would you still have become the Aglaea you are today?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Look at those broken, pleading eyes... how disappointing. We overestimated your cunning.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: If this plan fails, we still have dozens of splendid parting gifts prepared... Demigod, would you like to hear about them?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: ...I thought I could buy some more time.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: In these one thousand years... I've witnessed the fall of ten Titans. From my naive arrogance at the beginning to slowly learning how to guide others...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Now... it's time to let go. I should be grateful... grateful that I've reached this moment — to let my departure become a path for others to follow.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Have I done enough? If I embrace that prophecy now and sink into the warmth of these waters...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...will the wandering wind stop to mourn me, Cifera?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: A millennium ago at Marmoreal Market...

Stay on course. I'll contact Tribbie and ask her to keep the citizens calm. We'll hurry back to Okhema as fast as possible and assess the situation in the city. If we run into any enemies along the way...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Seamstress, I've come as promised! Look at this box full of gold and silver treasures. I bet there's stuff here you've never seen!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Come on, as we agreed, I want to buy the most valuable clothes you have!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Little thief, you've got some nerve, barging into my shop dressed in those tattered rags!
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: What have you brought? Let me see.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Here, take a look! Only the finest goods — see this sapphire? It's even more blue than Phagousa's eyes!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Such exquisite luster... I've only seen an Ocean's Tear of this quality in my mother's treasury...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Wait, you've seen one before? And here I thought I'd leave you speechless. Ugh, what a letdown.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: It's just an old memory. My family estate all burned to ashes long ago. This workshop is what I built from scratch.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Wow, a daughter rebuilding her family business — how admirable... Heh, enough with the jokes. At least you did get to enjoy those luxuries.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Heh... Mind your manners, kitty.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Tell me, Cifera, where did you come from, and how did you acquire these treasures?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Ha, I won them fair and square in a bet. What, do you doubt me?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Speak up, seamstress! Give me a straight answer. Do you want these or not?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Strange, you're clearly lying to my face...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: But my golden thread... doesn't tremble at all.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: That's because I'm not lying. I've been telling the truth from the start.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Is that so? But the scars and mud stains on your face tell another story.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Oh come on, can't we just do business without all this chatter? Don't worry, I didn't leave any evidence, so no one will bother you.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: How can I trust a word you say when you're so skilled at lying?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Dealing with you rich people is such a pain, always wasting my time! Fine, if you don't want it, there are plenty of others who do...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: ...Hold on.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Your treasure — I'll accept it. But these alone aren't enough to purchase the Goldweaver's finest clothes.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: That said, I do have something that would suit you perfectly.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Oh? What do you have in mind?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Look. Come a bit closer.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Oh! It's... shimmering gold, absolutely stunning!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: These golden boots are the Goldweaver's greatest treasures. Though not as valuable as the most precious gowns, they hold a magical power.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Legend has it that {RUBY_B#Trickery Titan}Zagreus{RUBY_E#} blessed these boots, allowing anyone who wears them to move swiftly and silently...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Put them on, Cifera, and don't get caught again. A face as lovely as yours deserves better protection.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Hmph, you rich folks just love sticking your noses in everything, don't you? Well, I'm taking these now, so don't get any second thoughts!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Uhh... hmm...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: What's wrong?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Uh... do you have a smaller size? These are way too big for me...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: ...Well, I suppose you'll have to grow into them.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Fake! Fake!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: ...Do you have to interrupt me in the middle of my story? Fake? What's fake?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Those boots definitely don't hold Zagreus's divine power!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: You're Amphoreus's most cunning liar, and even you were fooled by Aglaea — hehehe!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Watch your mouth, or I'll feed you to the fish in the River of Souls!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Weren't you curious how I got tangled up with that seamstress? Well, now you know. Satisfied?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Hehe... I didn't expect such a simple story. How disappointing.
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Huh?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: ...You're defending her?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Uh... no, no! I just think the story's so moving... it'd be a shame to ruin it with a lie. If I could cry, I'd be in tears right now!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Ha! Good thing you've still got a sharp tongue, or you'd have been stuck guarding someone's front door ages ago.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Enough chit-chat. Let's take a look at this place. The city of Styxia — look how beautiful she is!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Let me take a good sniff of this air...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Prrrrrr~~
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: This air... it's filled with the scent of treasure everywhere! Wonderful, just wonderful!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Thanks to Castorice and Gray Mystery, the ancient city's barrier was finally dispelled. Now that I think about it, helping them was well worth it.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Time for treasure hunting, Bartho! Lead the way, and whatever we find, we'll split 80-20.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Uh, well, I have a suggestion... How about 70-30 instead?
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: ...Listen closely. Do you hear that? The gnawfish in the River of Souls are growling with hunger...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: ...80-20 it is! How generous you are, Boss Lady Cipher!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Hehe, the mighty demigod of Trickery... uneasy around water?
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: You wouldn't understand! The people of Dolos are talented in many ways, just... not in swimming.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Why don't we have a race? Long-distance, sprint, or laps — take your pick!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Hehe, what's got you so worked up? Relax, relax... Who would've thought the fearless Lady Cipher was afraid of water!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Cats hate getting wet. What's so hard to understand about that?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Now hurry up and figure out a way across, or I might have to reconsider our split!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Uh... don't rush me. Let me take a look around...
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Got it — let's use that thing! Come on! Follow me, Boss Lady!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: (Hmph... Not a good imitation.)
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: (I'll play along... Let's see where this goes, "Bartholos.")
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Tell me... how did you hunt for treasure when I wasn't around, Boss Lady?
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Hmph, trying to trick me into saying something? Not a chance.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Hehe, you're as sharp as ever...
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Hehe, interesting, very interesting...
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Was this device designed by priests of Oronyx? Do you think you can handle it?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Don't underestimate me, Boss! Just find a cozy, dry corner and wait for me, hehe...
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Mission accomplished! Now you don't have to worry about your tail getting wet.
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Not bad. But just a warning — if this thing fails while we're halfway through the water...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Don't worry. Trust me! For that sweet 20% cut of the loot, I'll make sure you're taken care of!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Huh... this feels truly magical... When did you pick up this trick?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Uh... self-taught, all self-taught!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: We're here! Can we turn off this spotlight now? It's really blinding.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: No problem! Just use the device over there to shut it off.
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: The scent of gold coins, gems, and fine leather... it's so refreshing!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: The treasures in this ancient city are all floating back up thanks to Gray Mystery and that pink squirrel!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Boss Lady, we're set to make a fortune this time. Got any plans on how to spend it?
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Of course — spend nothing. Have you forgotten my silly prophecy?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Ah... I remember, of course! Hehehe...
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Oh! Isn't that my...
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: ...Uh-huh?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: ...Ahem, isn't that a controller for the Hand of Zagreus?
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Ho, indeed it is.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Once activated, this thing makes a racket that can be heard for miles — just too stupid! What was—...
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Ahem... Seriously, what was the Titan thinking when they came up with this thing?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Hey! If you don't want the "Trickery" to be exposed, you'd better start by keeping your mouth shut... What do you say?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Uh... hehe, Boss Lady, you're absolutely right! I'll be careful with my words!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: This thing's way too loud when it's on... Let's not stir up more trouble, okay?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Here we go round the River of Souls~
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Spirithief goes, Spirithief goes~
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: ...What are you even singing? You're totally out of tune!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Ho, there's a big guy guarding this place!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Yeah, yeah... big and dumb, just a pure lump of stupidity!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Need to make sure you don't die before you pay me.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Doot... Doot-Doot!
rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: Oh. Got it. Yes, I'll focus and not run off.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Look at its face — oh my, how could something be so ugly? Tsk tsk...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Yeah, yeah, so ugly... ugly enough to make even me, a little imp without a digestive system, feel nauseous!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Hyacine used the Chroma Coffer to summon the heroic spirit of the ancestor...
Hyacine used the Chroma Coffer to summon the heroic spirit of the ancestor...
If that ugly brute messes up my face, even the stoic Talanton might end up shedding a tear.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Hyacine used the Chroma Coffer to summon the heroic spirit of the ancestor...
...You like calling me that, don't you? Well, I've embraced it now. It doesn't even faze me anymore!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Hahaha... always dependable. I just hope you didn't lose any sleep. We've still got a tough fight ahead.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Since you're here, make yourself comfortable. You can take a nap while we're waiting for everyone else.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Ready, comrade? If all goes according to plan... this could be the last battle where we fight at each other's side.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Really? That's the first time I've heard that...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Ah... sorry, I'm no help there.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...You sound a little insincere there, buddy.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That would be a problem... We'll need to get you home before Era Nova.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Well, then I have to use something else Dan Heng taught me as come back — "The last mile is the hardest."
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "The last mile is the hardest." — That's from Dan Heng. Same principle, just... more elegantly put.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hey, speaking of Dan Heng... where is he?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Ha... After all this time, you should know when I'm just being polite and when I'm genuinely speaking from the heart.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: So full of energy, comrades. Seems I chose the perfect day.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Indeed, that would be heartbreaking! Clearly, running away is the sensible choice, hehe...
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: So, how about you take the front? I'll attack from the side.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Right, right. Fleeing fits our rogue nature...
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Doot... Doot-Doot.
rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: Hand of Zagreus, my darling — activate!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Hehe! Works like a charm!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Doot-Doot! Doot!
rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: Hmm...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Ha, not bad! However, I still don't see how this ties into "Trickery."
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Let's go, to the next trove!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Doot-Doot... Doot?
rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: Hey, slow down. That question you asked me earlier... I think I just remembered something.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: ...Eh? What did I ask?
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: You know... that question. The one you specifically asked me, right after we dug up the second chest.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Uh... forgive me, Boss Lady, but have you been under a lot of stress lately? I didn't ask anything. You must've imagined it!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Oh... is that so?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Maybe you're right. I have been a little on edge lately. I need to relax... Alright, let's move on to the next treasure trove.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Treasure! Let's go!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Twinkle, twinkle, in my chest~ How this Coreflame is the best!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: When it comes to singing, I still sound better than you, Boss!
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: ...Go beyond all time and space~ On the Journey of Flame-Chase~
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Ooh, this scent... feels like something incredible is buried here.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Incredible indeed! Hehe, if even Boss Lady says so, how can I not be excited?
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Do I need to give instructions here? Get digging!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Bartholos activated excavation mode, uncovering something hidden beneath the earth...
...Heh?
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Oh, isn't this a Golden Scapegoat? Interesting! Looks like whoever buried this treasure wanted to play a little game with us.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Oh, isn't there a myth about this thing? "Those who feared fire became sheep, those who did not became human"...
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Sheep, humans — whatever. All I know is unlocking this gets us treasure. Here, this honor's all yours.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Puzzles and tricks are right up my alley! Just leave it to little ol' me.
rows.speaker: "Spirithief" Bartholos

rows.text: Tsk...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: These folks in black...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Are not responding to provocations, nor do they seem intent on fighting. What exactly are they waiting for?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Pressure. Fear. Planting seeds of anxiety. It seems this is the strategy they've chosen.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: An organization that sees it as their mission to eradicate the Chrysos Heirs...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I've read some chilling accounts, stories of the "Cleaners" using alchemical arts to implant fragments of memories into their successors, ensuring both identity and hatred live on.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: From what I know, these stories are true. The Caenis we know today — strictly speaking — is the 27th Caenis.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Objectively, the rise of the Cleaners was both inevitable and necessary. Yet, their ruthless and twisted methods earned them nothing but disdain and condemnation from history.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: And still, they endure. An organization persisting through time, now working tirelessly to obstruct the Flame-Chase.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Are they truly so terrified of the "Era Nova" the Chrysos Heirs strive for?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Even in these crumbling end times, there are always those who find ways to profit from the chaos.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: To ask the vested interests to abandon their status, wealth, and ambitions in this world for a distant ideal, may be no easier than creating a miracle.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Is that... Lord Krateros?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There you are, Lord Dan Heng. We couldn't reach you on the teleslate, so the Holy City Guard almost assumed you and [Trailblazer] had met some terrible fate.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: You pests crawling in the shadows, back off! Your plot ends here.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: You've played your hand. Run while you still can. It might be your only chance to survive.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Stay away from Okhema forever. If you set foot there again, the fury of its people will tear you apart.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Because Aglaea is dead, and in the eyes of the holy city's citizens, her blood is on your hands!
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Bro, you sound so cool.
Bro, you sound kind of scary.
Phainon is seriously upset...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: But they were after the Chrysos Heirs.
Do they think they have a chance?
Hmm. I guess, the opposition within the Council of Elders is still desperately fighting to obstruct the Flame-Chase.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Probably a desperate gamble... I guess, the opposition within the Council of Elders is still desperately fighting to obstruct the Flame-Chase Journey.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: If the conspiracy is exposed, they'll be hunted down in the holy city like rats with nowhere to run. No matter where they hide...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Doot-Doot... Doot?
rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: Aglaea!? Is this —
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Blast it! Those guys...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It must be a lie...
Was it those guys' doing?
I've heard from more than one person. It doesn't seem like a joke.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But how could they possibly...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Stay calm... this could just be one of her schemes. I won't believe it until I see it for myself...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Phainon...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: What should we do now?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Doot! Doot-Doot!
rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: ...I won't be merciful this time.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "...Chartonus."
Mmm...?
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: "You're forging a sword for Phainon, aren't you?"
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: "I haven't seen you wield the hammer in so long... I couldn't help but be entranced by the sight."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: You... Aglaea.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: In this form, you come to me. It means...
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: "That's right. At this moment, my physical form is already shattered. My journey as a human in this world has come to an end."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: "It's time to fulfill our pact."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: Of course... The pact, I haven't forgotten.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: "The thing I entrusted to you, do you still have it?"
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: Far too plain, this vessel is... Not worthy of you. Do you still insist?
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: "I insist."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: "Over the past thousand years, every piece of fabric I've worked with has been tainted by my cold divinity. It's made me hate their colors, texture, and scent."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: "This ornament stands apart... It was a gift from a child. She was pure and kind. I often wished my childhood could have been like hers."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: How to say goodbye to everyone... have you already planned?
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: "I'm afraid there's no such detailed plan this time. I deeply regret not being able to say farewell to them one by one."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: "The moment has come... My departure will give them one less thing to worry about. This parting gift should help ease the regret of such a sudden goodbye."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: Invented for the Titans, Kremnos's Soul-Forging technology was. Though divinity it retains, filtered out, the remnants of humanity will be.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Is that what you want, Aglaea?
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: "You've confirmed this with me repeatedly. Yes, Chartonus, I need you to do this for me."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: "Condense my divinity into this ornament... It might still be useful in the future to help them complete their mission."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: Selfless, until the end.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Envy that child, there's no need to... Already lived a grand life, your humanity has.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Now, the next ancestor on the list... her spirit is said to rest in the Vortex of Genesis. A pity that the ceremony has to be performed in strict order. Shall we head back to Okhema together, Dannie?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: The Vortex of Genesis, huh...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I have a suggestion.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hmm...?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Remember how you suggested I learn the "secret arts of water" from Phagousa's priests?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I've been practicing that in my spare time and made some progress. Now, as long as I have spirit water with me, I can use those techniques to carve a path directly to the Vortex of Genesis.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Ah, I remember! I didn't expect you to keep at it this long — that's so like you, Dannie.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Compared to the currents of my home, the waters of Amphoreus are... rather untamed. Subduing the waters wasn't easy, but I've gotten the hang of it now.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That makes sense. {RUBY_B#Ocean Titan}Phagousa{RUBY_E#} was always described as a fickle Titan in the myths.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Since you're offering... then let me put your skills to the test, Dannie.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: The spirit water gate formed with this technique isn't as stable as a ritual basin. It'll likely only let one person through.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: And as Phagousa's priests designed it — "the entrance serves as the exit." You'll need to come back through the vortex once you've met your ancestor's spirit. Little Ica and I will be here waiting.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Doot... Doot-Doot!
rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: Got it. I'm counting on you, Dannie!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: "...Under the raucous steps of their frenzied dance, the roar of celebration hides the world's heartbeat."
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: "Spirit water, reveal the way —"
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: "Heh... your praise puts my heart at ease, Grand Craftsman. Now..."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: "...please take me through the last tempering that fate has to offer."
rows.speaker: Golden Nymph

rows.text: The city is silent, and tension is building with every passing second.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The news has probably spread by now. Every household is locked up tight... and all the market stalls have closed down temporarily.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: She really was taken by the Cleaners...
Something about this feels like a scheme...
Unless it's all a part of her plan.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I just can't believe she'd be taken down by a handful of assassins...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let's go find her.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Dan Heng came back before us.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Maybe he's heard something...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Ah, you're back. How's everything? No injuries, I hope?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Don't worry. The Cleaners didn't lay a hand on us.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Lord Krateros, were you in the city when it happened? What exactly went down...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Regrettably, no one knows the details of that moment.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Eyewitnesses only saw... um...
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: ...It's fine. Just tell me.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Eyewitnesses at the Marmoreal Palace saw Aglaea fall from the Chrysos Heir Bath.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Oh gods...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: She showed no signs of life by the time the Holy City Guards approached to check.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: They were too afraid to jump to conclusions... After all, she was a demigod who'd lived for over a thousand years, the leader of the Chrysos Heirs. Most citizens of this city believed that death couldn't touch her.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: She was pierced through the heart by a uniquely crafted dagger. I saw it for myself. It's one of the weapons carried by the "Cleaners."
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Why didn't they go after us?
She really was assassinated...
They didn't have any reason, nor the courage, to attack Aglaea. Perhaps...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: Got it. I'm counting on you, Dannie!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: "...Under the raucous steps of their frenzied dance, the roar of celebration hides the world's heartbeat."
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: "Spirit water, reveal the way —"
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Speculating blindly won't help. Let's go find Lady Tribbie, as she understands Aglaea's mind best.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Thank you, Lord Krateros.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The baths are empty...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No citizen feels like bathing after hearing such terrible news.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hyacine.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...You're back!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: We heard from Krateros. Are you... alright?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'm fine... I've been staying close to Lady Tribbie and Lady Trinnon after the incident.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Cut Snowy some slack, Ciphy. He's still so young, yet he's shouldering all the responsibilities Agy left behind...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: It's great that you could come back so quickly... They need someone with them now.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: How are the two of them holding up?
You witnessed Aglaea's...
Declaring her death was the hardest thing I've ever had to do as a doctor.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Lord Phainon... don't push yourself. You're carrying a heavier burden now. Please don't fall...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: ...It's fine. I can handle it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What I've lost is a mentor, and a comrade-in-arms. But for Tribbie and Trinnon, they've lost a thousand-year-old bond... like losing a part of their lives.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You should rest, Hyacine. You've been awake for a long time, haven't you? We'll handle things from here.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Okay. See you later, everyone.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Next... we should visit Lady Tribbie.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Snowy, Little Gray... you're back.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Lady Tribbie, I...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Snowy, don't! Please don't apologize to us.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: You went to the Grove to prepare yourself for the threats to Okhema. You didn't do anything wrong, so don't be hard on yourself.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: We were always by Agy's side throughout this long journey, so we understood her thoughts better than anyone.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: She knew she wouldn't see the end of the Flame-Chase Journey, yet she gave everything without hesitation... for the future of everyone.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: I know what Aglaea expected of me. Right now, the last thing Okhema needs is a leader wallowing in self-pity.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The scroll over there was entrusted to us by Agy. She instructed us to hand it over to you when the time was right.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: I think... now's the "right time."
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: I still remember the taste of that oatmeal...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: See you tomorrow morning. I'll prepare breakfast for you then.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: I planned to get everything settled before coming to see you. Is there something urgent, Chartonus?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: How you're holding up, I wanted to see.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Better than I expected, you seem.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: There's no room for doubt anymore. It's time to take action and show everyone that the leadership of the Chrysos Heirs is still strong.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Right, your assessment is. Now, here, take this.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Is this... You've completed it?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "Dawnmaker" — the name I've chosen for it.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Doot-Doot! Doot!
rows.speaker: Little Ica

rows.text: Before Dawn, prepare for battle. For tomorrow, wield your sword. Befits your stature, it does, Chrysos Heir.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: "Dawnmaker"...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Unbelievable. You've never seen that black-clad swordmaster... yet you've recreated this so precisely, just from what I described?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Precise, your description.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Imbued it with the power of Dawn, I already have. Guided by your will, gleam with golden flames, its blade will.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Wield it. May triumph always be yours.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Thank you, Chartonus. I will use this sword to protect the beings of Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Another thing, there is...
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: What's this...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Stored here, the remnants of Aglaea's divinity are.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: This was her commission. Her death, she had long foreseen.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Can she still hear us?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's difficult to confirm. About divinity, we know very little.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: In this way, she wanted to be with you, always.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: I understand. Let me keep it. With this... I'll have another constant companion by my side.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "May this world never have need for a Deliverer." Someone told me long ago.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But when the world dashed her hopes and fell into disarray, if she could see me now — leading from the front, rallying people against their destiny...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...She would surely smile.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: How will the holy city continue without Lady Goldweaver...
rows.speaker: Pessimistic Citizen

rows.text: ...Look! Lord Phainon is here.
rows.speaker: Uneasy Citizen

rows.text: Will he step up to lead Okhema?
rows.speaker: Hesitant Citizen

rows.text: Not long ago, I spoke at the citizens' assembly at Dawncloud.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I wrestled with every word, searching for the right ones to rally support and keep the Chrysos Heirs' Flame-Chase alive.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: In the end, I remembered a lesson from one of my teachers: In battles where words are weapons, outrage and blind passion often overpower reason.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I followed his strategy. I painted my opponents as nothing more than pests, tore apart their character, and laid out their crimes.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The strategy worked. I secured enough votes to achieve my goal. But afterward? There wasn't even a flicker of joy.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I realized — that apparent victory masked a deeper failure. In my pursuit of success, I fueled division and strayed far from my very purpose that led me to the Flame-Chase Journey.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: This journey was supposed to unify, not divide. To strengthen us, not weaken us.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It was the gold thread that mended our rifts in the past. Some saw it as a means of surveillance, a tool of control, but no one can deny that it was Aglaea who held this city, and even this shattered world, together.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Now she is gone — yes, as you have heard — the demigod Aglaea, who guarded the holy city for a millennium, has indeed fallen.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Who murdered Lady Goldweaver?
rows.speaker: Furious Citizen

rows.text: Find the murderer! Make them pay!
rows.speaker: Righteous Citizen

rows.text: I felt the same as all of you initially.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...But my perspective has changed.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The golden threads that once bound this city have unraveled, yet no one is celebrating their freedom from control. In the empty markets and bath chambers, one feeling lingers: Unease.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Deep down, we all know — the last safeguard against the harm we may do to each other is gone. No divine power will protect us from the malice in our hearts. From now on, only the moral code we choose to uphold for ourselves will stand between us and the abyss.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Phainon has a way with words.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...I will join the heroes of the prophecy to return to the sky and retrieve the Coreflame.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Ancestor, please bestow upon me your generous blessing...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Witness Hyacine collect blessings from afar.
Before I rise to the skies, I challenge you — cast out the shadows and malice within your hearts. Let your spirits shine brighter than the sky itself!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let me bear witness: Even without the divine authority of Romance, Okhema will remain a sanctuary in these end times. A place for the kind people Aglaea dreamed of, the kind of people foretold in prophecy...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: A better people!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Better people!
rows.speaker: Spirited Citizen

rows.text: Better people! Better people!
rows.speaker: Inspired Citizens

rows.text: Better people! Better people! Better people!
rows.speaker: Okheman

rows.text: I appreciate your willingness to accept the challenge... You have reminded me that Aglaea left me perhaps the simplest duty in the world.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: To bear the burden of creation, I need only to give one thing. It's a gift she once gave me without hesitation, and now I share it with each of you — unshakable faith.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: There's still a long way to go before Amphoreus is reborn. But we will not forget the past as we move forward, for the memories of Amphoreus will always benefit future generations.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Allow me this moment. I want to borrow a few minutes of your time to commemorate a demigod who protected the holy city for a millennium...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...She was Okhema's dressmaker, the leader of the Chrysos Heirs, the Goldweaver Aglaea. And her greatest feat —
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: — was being a selfless person.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That singing sounds so familiar!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: That's our song, and Snowy used to love it!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Yes, Lady Trianne. For that child filled with anxiety...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...your songs always dispelled the clouds in my heart, even if just for a moment.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hehe... Snowy was so cute and kind when he was little!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Now... hmm, you've grown so much. Maybe not as cute but still just as kind!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Hahaha... Time spares no one, so there's nothing we can do. But kindness... you helped nurture it in me.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Don't mention it! Your light is as bright as ever. Keep it up and stay strong!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: See you, Snowy.
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Goodbye, Lady Trianne.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I heard what you said. Are you suggesting the debate tactics I've taught you are nothing but sleight of hand?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Not at all, Professor Anaxa. Honestly, without those techniques you taught me, the Flame-Chase Journey might not have survived.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hmph... Good thing your head's still clear.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The Chrysos Heir of Kephale... I had no idea you had it in you while I was drilling those formulas in your head in class.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Legend tells of the Skyfolk once divided into many tribes.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: The Sunfolk worshiped the sun, the Rainfolk were devoted to storms, and the Winterfolk waited for signs in the snow...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Our ancestors lived under Aquila's light, yet they were blinded to all but one color.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: They forgot that... the light that illuminates the world is made of countless different colors.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: That's why the rainbow is my favorite, for not only does it reflect the many colors, it is also a bridge.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: And I want to use the rainbow bridge to link everyone's hearts... and give hope to every soul on earth.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Ancestors!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: With the rainbow as your guide, lead me back to the home of the Skyfolk, a land we have not seen for a thousand years!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Flying along the Rainbow Bridge is truly an amazing experience.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The Eye of Twilight...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's the legendary sky fortress of {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#} — I never imagined that one day I'd be able to step foot on it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: My ancestors once built a magnificent civilization among the heavens. The Eye of Twilight, which we are standing on, is the home of Aquila and the heart of the city-state in the clouds.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: This must be where the hero Seliose stood when she challenged Aquila and began the first step of the Flame-Chase Journey...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: We are here to end the journey she began.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: But they were divided within. The frequent wars started by the Chrysos Heirs drained their power, especially after the prophecy descended. In the end, they had to hide among the clouds, far from the conflicts raging below.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Apparently, the division was between the two most important sky tribes, the Sunfolk and the Rainfolk.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: And Seliose's frustration towards the endless strife among her people made her turn her spear towards the Titan above.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: In other words, she became one with the Titan... I would have considered it a fairytale, but after seeing what happened with Professor Anaxa? Not anymore.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Has that Titan... and that fused hero... been looking down on the world from here for a thousand years?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Something's not right...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I can kind of feel how big and empty this place is, but all I see is darkness.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What's on the other side of this?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng
